justification: The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model.assembly shows good stability characteristics. It has a clear dependency on org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.core for constants and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.util for utilities, which are likely more stable foundational packages. The assembly package contains specialized parsers for different architectures (x86, ARM) and related classes that form a cohesive unit for assembly processing. Dependencies are primarily on standard Java libraries (java.util, java.io, java.lang) and well-established external libraries (com.chrisnewland.freelogj for logging, org.xml.sax for XML parsing). The package structure demonstrates good encapsulation with interfaces (IAssemblyParser) and abstract classes (AbstractAssemblyParser) providing stable contracts. There are no indications of unstable dependencies where less stable packages depend on more stable ones - the dependencies flow toward foundational, more stable packages.

The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.compilationchooser has minimal outgoing dependencies, only importing core JavaFX classes and a few interfaces from the same project (org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.main and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model). It does not depend on any less stable packages. The package is itself a UI component with low complexity and clear separation of concerns, indicating stability. There are no incoming dependencies from less stable packages that would violate the Stable Dependencies Principle.

The package com.google.zxing.aztec depends on com.google.zxing.common and com.google.zxing, both of which are more stable foundational packages. The aztec package implements specific Aztec code functionality and correctly depends on more stable, lower-level components like common utilities and core classes. There are no dependencies on less stable packages, adhering to the Stable Dependencies Principle.

The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.report has outgoing dependencies on org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.treevisitor, which are more stable packages as they contain core model classes and interfaces. There are no incoming dependencies from less stable packages that would violate the Stable Dependencies Principle. The package depends on more stable components (model, treevisitor) and does not exhibit unstable dependency.

The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.process.runtime contains runtime implementation classes (RuntimeJava, RuntimeScala, etc.) that depend on AbstractProcess and IRuntime from the same package, and on logger and process packages which are more stable utility components. The dependencies flow from concrete runtime implementations to more abstract and stable components, following the Stable Dependencies Principle. There are no dependencies on less stable packages.

The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.stage has minimal outgoing dependencies (primarily to javafx.stage.Stage) and no significant incoming dependencies from other packages shown in the code. It primarily contains UI-related classes (IStageClosedListener, StageManager) that manage stage lifecycle events and communication. The dependencies are stable (JavaFX) and the package itself appears to be relatively stable with simple interfaces and manager classes. There are no signs of depending on less stable components.

The package com.google.zxing.client.android.history shows stable dependency characteristics. It primarily depends on core ZXing library classes (com.google.zxing.*) which are more stable than this package itself. The history package contains classes for managing scan history functionality including HistoryItem, HistoryManager, DBHelper, and HistoryActivity. Its dependencies flow towards more stable packages - it depends on the core ZXing library for barcode processing (Result, BarcodeFormat) and Android framework classes for UI and storage. The package does not exhibit unstable dependency patterns as it doesn't depend on less stable packages while being relatively unstable itself. The dependencies are properly directed from less stable to more stable components, following the Stable Dependencies Principle.

The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.parserchooser has stable dependencies. It only depends on the org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.parser package (via ParserType enum) which is more stable since it contains core parsing logic that changes less frequently than UI components. The parserchooser package itself contains simple UI components (interface and chooser class) with minimal complexity and few dependencies, making it relatively stable. There are no dependencies on less stable packages, thus no unstable dependency smell is detected.

The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.toplist does not exhibit the Unstable Dependency smell. It depends on several other packages including org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model, org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.compilation, org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.treevisitor, org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.intrinsic, org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.hotthrow, and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.util. These dependencies are stable components (model classes, utility classes, and core functionality) that are less likely to change frequently. The package itself appears to be a utility package for generating top lists and statistics, which typically depends on more stable core components. There are no indications that this package depends on less stable components in violation of the Stable Dependencies Principle.

The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.process.javap contains classes JavapProcess and ReflectionJavap. JavapProcess extends AbstractProcess which is not in the same package, but there's no evidence of instability in the dependency. ReflectionJavap uses classes from org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.loader (DisposableURLClassLoader) and com.chrisnewland.freelogj (Logger, LoggerFactory). However, these dependencies do not indicate that the package depends on less stable components. The package appears to have stable dependencies as it depends on well-established logging and utility classes, and does not show signs of violating the Stable Dependencies Principle.

The package com.packageName contains classes that are only depended upon by other classes (in the default package) but do not depend on any external packages themselves. Specifically, classes like ClassInPackage and InnerStaticClassFieldContainer are used by classes in the default package, but com.packageName does not have any outgoing dependencies to less stable packages. Therefore, it does not exhibit an Unstable Dependency smell.

The package com.google.zxing.client.android.result.supplement depends on com.google.zxing.client.android.history and com.google.zxing.client.result. Both of these packages are more stable than the supplement package, as they contain core functionality and data models that are less likely to change frequently. The supplement package contains classes that retrieve additional information based on scan results, making it more volatile and less stable. Therefore, the dependencies follow the Stable Dependencies Principle, with the less stable package depending on more stable ones.

The package com.google.zxing.client.android.camera depends on android.graphics, android.hardware, android.os, android.util, android.view, java.util, java.util.regex, java.io, java.lang, and com.google.zxing. These are all more stable packages (Android SDK packages and Java standard library) or equally stable dependencies. The package does not depend on any less stable packages. It follows the Stable Dependencies Principle as it depends on more stable or equally stable components.

The package com.google.zxing.client.android.clipboard is a utility package that provides clipboard functionality. It has minimal dependencies, relying only on standard Android classes (android.content.ClipData, android.content.ClipboardManager, android.content.Context, android.util.Log). It does not depend on any other internal packages from the application. The package is stable due to its focused, utility nature and lack of complex dependencies. Since this package doesn't have outgoing dependencies to other less stable packages, it does not exhibit the Unstable Dependency smell.

The package com.google.zxing.pdf417.detector has dependencies on com.google.zxing and com.google.zxing.common packages. These dependencies are stable foundational packages of the ZXing library that provide core functionality like BinaryBitmap, ResultPoint, BitMatrix, NotFoundException, and DecodeHintType. The detector package itself is a specialized component for PDF417 barcode detection and follows the Stable Dependencies Principle by depending on more stable, core library components rather than less stable packages. Therefore, no unstable dependency smell is detected.

The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.parser.zing has incoming dependencies (used by other packages) but no outgoing dependencies to other packages within the provided code. It only depends on standard Java libraries (java.io, java.util, java.util.regex) and its own internal packages (org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.core, org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model, org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.parser, org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.util). Since it doesn't depend on any less stable packages and is itself a leaf package in terms of inter-package dependencies, it does not exhibit the Unstable Dependency smell.

The package org.apache.commons.io.file.spi has no outgoing dependencies to other packages within the codebase, and its stability is determined by its reliance only on standard Java libraries (java.net, java.nio.file, etc.). Since there are no inter-package dependencies violating the Stable Dependencies Principle, this is not an Unstable Dependency smell.

The package 'net.bytebuddy.benchmark.specimen' contains only two classes, 'ExampleClass' and 'ExampleInterface', which are simple specimen classes used for benchmarking. These classes do not have any outgoing dependencies to other packages, and there are no incoming dependencies from other packages that would create unstable dependency relationships. The package is stable as it has no external dependencies that could cause instability.

The package org.apache.commons.lang3.event has stable dependencies. It depends on org.apache.commons.lang3.reflect.MethodUtils and org.apache.commons.lang3.exception.ExceptionUtils which are stable utility classes within the same library (Apache Commons Lang3). These dependencies are more stable than the event package itself since they provide fundamental utility functions. There are no dependencies on less stable packages, and the dependencies follow the Stable Dependencies Principle.

The package org.gradle.work only contains placeholder classes (ChangeType, FileChange, InputChanges) that represent Gradle's API types. These classes have no outgoing dependencies on other packages - they only contain basic method signatures without implementations. The package also has no incoming dependencies shown from other packages in the provided code. Since there are no actual dependencies between packages, there is no unstable dependency smell to detect.

The package 'com.google.gson.internal.bind.util' contains only the 'ISO8601Utils' class which is a utility class for date formatting and parsing. It does not have any outgoing dependencies on other packages within the provided code context, and no other packages depend on it. Since there are no dependencies to analyze for stability violations, there is no unstable dependency smell detected.

The package org.gradle.api.file does not exhibit unstable dependency. It has minimal outgoing dependencies, only depending on java.io.File and org.gradle.api.provider.Provider. It does not depend on any other packages with higher instability. The package is relatively stable as it contains only interface definitions (DirectoryProperty, Directory) with no complex dependencies or implementations that would introduce instability.

The package com.google.zxing.aztec.detector depends on com.google.zxing.aztec.AztecDetectorResult and several classes in com.google.zxing.common and com.google.zxing.common.reedsolomon. These dependencies are more stable as they are foundational classes used across multiple packages in the library. AztecDetectorResult extends DetectorResult, which is a stable base class. The Reed-Solomon classes are also stable utility classes for error correction. The detector package itself contains specialized detection logic, making it less stable than the packages it depends on, thus following the Stable Dependencies Principle.

The package com.google.zxing.integration.android contains only two classes, IntentIntegrator and IntentResult, which are designed to integrate with the ZXing barcode scanning library. The IntentIntegrator class depends on standard Android SDK classes (Activity, Fragment, Intent, etc.) and Java standard library classes (Collections, HashMap, etc.). These dependencies are stable and part of the core platform. There are no dependencies on other less stable packages or components. The package follows the Stable Dependencies Principle as it depends only on more stable components (Android SDK and Java standard library).

The package 'com.google.gson.protobuf' containing 'ProtoTypeAdapter' depends on 'com.google.gson' and 'com.google.protobuf'. Both of these are more stable libraries (Gson is a core JSON library and Protobuf is a Google standard for serialization). The 'ProtoTypeAdapter' is designed to bridge these two stable libraries, and it does not depend on less stable components. It adheres to the Stable Dependencies Principle by depending on more stable packages.

The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.resize contains the RateLimitedResizeListener and IRedrawable interface. Classes in other packages (org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.nmethod, org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.graphing, org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.compilechain) depend on these classes. The resize package itself has no outgoing dependencies to other packages, making it a stable component that other less stable components depend on. This follows the Stable Dependencies Principle, as stable components should be depended upon, not depend on others. Therefore, there is no Unstable Dependency smell.

The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.histo does not exhibit Unstable Dependency. It depends on stable components such as org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model, org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.compilation, and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.treevisitor. These dependencies are more stable as they contain core model classes and interfaces that are less likely to change frequently. The package itself appears to be a utility package for creating histograms, which suggests a stable role within the system.

The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.nmethod.compilerthread has outgoing dependencies on org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.nmethod, and incoming dependencies from org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.main. The stability of the dependent packages (model being more stable/core, ui.nmethod being at the same UI level, and ui.main being a higher-level UI component) follows a logical flow where this package depends on more stable packages (model) and is depended upon by less stable packages (ui.main), which aligns with the Stable Dependencies Principle and does not indicate an Unstable Dependency smell.

The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.chain has a stable dependency architecture. It depends on more stable packages like org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model (which contains core data structures) and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.util (which contains utility functions). The chain package is less stable than these dependencies, following the Stable Dependencies Principle. Classes in this package (CompileNode, CompileChainWalker) are used by UI components (CompileChainStage) but don't create unstable dependency cycles.

The package com.google.zxing.oned.rss contains classes that are part of a cohesive module for reading RSS family barcodes. The classes within this package have high cohesion as they all relate to RSS barcode processing. The package depends on com.google.zxing.common and com.google.zxing.common.detector for shared utilities like BitArray, BitMatrix, MathUtils, and detector classes, which are stable foundational components. These dependencies are stable because they provide basic data structures and common utilities that are unlikely to change frequently. The package does not depend on less stable packages; instead, it depends on more stable ones. Therefore, it follows the Stable Dependencies Principle and does not exhibit the Unstable Dependency smell.

The package org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.hotthrow depends on org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.compilation. The model package contains core data structures and is likely more stable due to its foundational nature. The compilation package, while containing utility classes, appears to be part of the same architectural layer and likely has similar or lower stability. Since the hotthrow package depends on packages that are equally or less stable, it does not violate the Stable Dependencies Principle. There is no evidence of dependency on less stable packages that would constitute an Unstable Dependency smell.

The package com.github.javaparser.storage contains only the PrimaryType class with no visible outgoing dependencies to other packages. Without outgoing dependencies to less stable packages, there is no unstable dependency smell detected.
